findings.note: internal/fsm/mockai/mockai.go:153 — `// LoadHash is the machine.Deps.MockLoad adapter.` asserts a wiring role the function does not fill. No caller outside the package exists (repo-wide grep for LoadHash hits only this file, mockai_test.go, and historical review docs); the CLI instead re-implements the same three lines inline at internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:197-203 while binding cli.Deps.MockLoad to mockai.Load (cli/deps.go:72). So this is dead exported production code, a duplicated code path (rubric: "the change appears to duplicate an inventoried service or code path"), and a false claim about the system's wiring. It is also the one function in the package whose 100%-statement coverage comes purely from a test of code the product never runs (mockai_test.go:46,52,80). Fix by deleting LoadHash and its assertions, or by having wiring.go call it instead of duplicating it — and correcting the comment either way.

findings.note: internal/fsm/mockai/mockai.go:241-252 — the 512 KB cap is enforced after the whole file is already in memory. The comment ("caps judge.yaml … the peek reads it before the run is verified") and both specs (fsm-cli.md:440 "judge.yaml read capped at 512 KB", fsm-judge-kinds.md:336 "caps the judge.yaml read at 512 KB") describe a capped read; os.ReadFile at line 246 is unbounded, so a multi-gigabyte judge.yaml under --mock-ai is fully read before ERR_MOCK_INVALID{too_large} can fire. An io.LimitReader(fh, MaxFileBytes+1) would make the code match the claim, as machine/sidecar.go:96 and cli/run.go:169 already do. Partly mitigating: the goldens cap (machine/machine.go:267) uses the same post-hoc pattern, so this is an existing repo idiom rather than a new regression, and the path requires an operator-supplied in-repo scenario dir.

evidence.note: os.ReadFile is unbounded; the len(raw) > MaxFileBytes check at line 250 runs only afterwards.

findings.note: internal/fsm/mockai/mockai.go:245-258 — "Load reads <dir>/judge.yaml strictly" overstates the strictness. dec.KnownFields(true) plus one Decode rejects unknown and duplicate keys but reads only the FIRST YAML document; everything after a `---` separator is discarded with no error. Reproduced against gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1 with this exact struct and decoder configuration: a two-document input returned only document 1's calls and no cmds, err=nil. Because Hash() covers all the bytes, a scenario can hash as pinned while half of it is silently inert, surfacing later as ERR_MOCK_UNSCRIPTED with no pointer to the cause. A trailing `dec.Decode(&extra)` that requires io.EOF would close it. Related nit on the same call: an empty or comment-only judge.yaml is rejected with detail "EOF", which is opaque next to the other ERR_MOCK_INVALID details.

evidence.note: Single Decode over a yaml.Decoder; subsequent documents never read.

findings.note: internal/fsm/mockai/mockai.go:298 — fakeRunner.Run discards the context, so a scenario-driven run never honours cancellation at the command boundary, contrary to the cmdexec.Runner interface contract at internal/fsm/cmdexec/cmdexec.go:60-64 ("a parent context cancellation is returned as ctx.Err()"); Guarded.exec (cmdexec.go:139) does no ctx check of its own. Impact is limited to mock/rehearsal runs and is largely absorbed by the machine-level ctx checks (machine/machine.go:656,889), so advisory: a leading `if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil { return cmdexec.Result{ExitCode: -1}, err }` would make the fake honour the interface it implements.
